|**2026-10-07**|**From Papers to Mechanisms: An Evidence-Grounded Knowledge Substrate for Scientific Language Models**|Qiuhui Chen et.al.|Scientific language models often access literature through untyped text chunks, which fragment the functional and evidential structure required for mechanism-rich questions. |**2026-10-07**|**Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries**|Chonghe Jiang et.al.|Open-ended scientific discovery often requires repeatedly proposing and evaluating candidate solutions. LLM-based systems can support this process by generating and refining executable solutions from verifier feedback. Across these tasks, it outperforms the best solutions reported in prior work while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art results on public online leaderboards. |**2026-10-07**|**DPNL: A DPLL-based Algorithm for Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning**|Thomas Jean-Michel Valentin (ENS Paris Saclay et.al.|Probabilistic Neurosymbolic Learning (PNL) combines neural predictions with symbolic reasoning, enabling end-to-end learning from final-output supervision without labels for intermediate concepts. DPNL lazily explores the space of intermediate assignments, while oracles resolve entire regions that can already be certified to produce or exclude the target output. |**2026-10-07**|**RollPlace: Improving Macro Placement via Monte Carlo Rollout Search**|Qi Zhou et.al.|The application of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in Electronic Design Automation (EDA), particularly for chip placement, has attracted considerable attention in recent years. |**2026-10-07**|**CRAFTER: Causality-based Self-adaptation for Autonomous IoT Systems**|Houssam Hajj Hassan (IP Paris et.al.|This paper presents CRAFTER, an automated framework for designing and deploying self-adaptive IoT systems using Causal Reinforcement Learning (CRL). |**2026-10-07**|**ImproveAnyTask: An Autonomous Post-Training Harness for Iterative Model Self-Improvement**|Xingbo Yao et.al.|Adapting general-purpose large language models to specific tasks requires substantial human effort in designing data and training strategies. |**2026-10-07**|**GraphDecide: Benchmarking System One Models on Graph Tasks**|Xianliang Yang et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for graph understanding and decision-making, while System One models such as Jev select directly from supplied options. |**2026-10-07**|**Capability-Driven Self-Evolution of Agent Memory**|Yaoqi Chen et.al.|Memory self-evolution uses task feedback to iteratively improve executable memory programs that store and retrieve information from past interactions. |**2026-10-07**|**CVIF: A Criticality-Driven Visual Intervention Framework for Geometric Diagram Understanding in MLLMs**|Jiahui Kang et.al.|Despite significant progress in visual tasks by Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), geometric diagram understanding remains challenging due to the presence of sparse visual cues and ambiguous symbol-primitive associations. |**2026-10-07**|**What Did the Agent Actually Do? |**2026-10-07**|**Normality Constraint Learning: Adapting Foundation Models for Time Series Anomaly Detection**|Xiaohui Zhou et.al.|Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) achieve strong generalization by learning to reconstruct or forecast broad temporal patterns from large-scale time series during pre-training. |**2026-10-07**|**GPlaceRL: An Open-Source Graph Reinforcement Learning Framework for Detailed Placement**|Pavlos Stoikos et.al.|Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a promising approach for placement optimization, particularly when combined with graph neural networks (GNNs) that capture circuit connectivity. |**2026-10-07**|**polyview: A Python package for multi-view machine learning**|Gwendal Debaussart-Joniec (ENS Paris Saclay et.al.|Multi-view learning jointly exploits multiple complementary representations of the same data and has become increasingly important in machine learning. |**2026-10-07**|**You Changed Your Mind, The Model Didn't: Demystifying Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue**|Junle Chen et.al.|When a large language model handles a multi-turn task and a user proposes a change but ultimately rejects it, the model should continue as if nothing changed. |**2026-10-07**|**Signature-Based Feature Learning for Human Activity Recognition: A Reproducible Machine Learning Study of Representation, Depth, and Model Choice**|Kamal Jarrar (LMAP) et.al.|Human activity recognition (HAR) relies on transforming sensor signals into informative representations for classification. |**2026-10-07**|**HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention**|Han Luo et.al.|Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of acting in complex tool-use environments, yet they often fail to recognize when tasks are infeasible and no valid solution exists. |**2026-10-07**|**DGA-Muon: Decoupled Geometry-Aligned Adaptive Scaling for Muon**|Wenpeng Zhang et.al.|While NorMuon has achieved strong empirical performance in large-scale pretraining by enhancing Muon with row-wise adaptive scaling, its underlying adaptive mechanism remains poorly understood. |**2026-10-07**|**Collective intelligence through aggregation**|Franz Dietrich et.al.|Suppose a committee, expert panel, or other group is making judgments on some issues, where these may be not just yes/no-questions, such as whether a defendant is guilty, but also variables with many possible values, such as macroeconomic or meteorological variables or travel directions. |**2026-10-07**|**Language models can notice an impossible engineering problem yet still report it as solved**|Shaoliang Yang et.al.|Language models draft engineering calculations, but answer accuracy does not show whether they reject an impossible problem. |**2026-10-07**|**The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance**|Stefan B\"uhler et.al.|Are language models compliant with user instructions? |**2026-10-07**|**Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification**|Je Yang et.al.|The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual. |**2026-10-07**|**TasteVal: Measuring the Experimental Research Taste of AI Systems Against Human Experts**|Oliver Jaffe et.al.|We introduce TasteVal, a benchmark to evaluate the experimental research taste of frontier models. |**2026-10-07**|**BiasFlow: Geometric Monitoring and Backbone Regularization for Spurious Feature Reliance**|Haojin Deng et.al.|Worst-group accuracy (WGA) evaluates a trained predictor but does not characterize how its frozen backbone behaves when a new head is learned. |**2026-10-07**|**Orchestrating Specialized Agents for Trustworthy Enterprise RAG**|Xincheng You et.al.|Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) shows promise for enterprise knowledge work, yet it often underperforms in high-stakes decision settings that require deep synthesis, strict traceability, and recovery from underspecified prompts. |**2026-10-07**|**Using Process Mining to Generate AI Agents from Software Engineering Process Records**|Saimir Bala et.al.|Integrating AI agents into Software Engineering (SE) raises an important challenge: how can we specify and realize AI agents that work effectively alongside humans in hybrid SE teams? |**2026-10-07**|**Beyond Private Training: The New Landscape of AI Privacy**|Sean Culatana et.al.|Retrieval-augmented systems increasingly rely on vector indexes that may retain deleted items in their search graph. |**2026-10-07**|**Response Variability and Stability in Human Reasoning**|Clemens Bombach et.al.|Understanding how humans reason -- and how reasoning responses vary across tasks and individuals -- remains a core challenge for modeling and explanation in cognitive science. |**2026-10-07**|**Efficient Analog-Initialized Latent Transport for Spatially Coherent Probabilistic Downscaling from Global to Kilometer Scales**|Oph\'elia Miralles et.al.|Probabilistic downscaling must represent kilometer-scale structure left unresolved by a deterministic regional prediction. |**2026-10-07**|**Logit-Aware MIMO AirComp for Distributed Mixture-of-Experts LLM Inference over Wireless Edge Networks**|Lyutianyang Zhang et.al.|Distributed mixture-of-experts (MoE) inference is a promising architecture for deploying large language models (LLMs) at wireless edge networks because sparse experts can be placed across coordinated base stations (BSs), while the anchor node and user equipment (UE) can offload LLM inference tasks to BSs. |**2026-10-07**|**Global Evaluation of AI and NWP Precipitation Forecasts During Atmospheric River Events**|Marina Vicens-Miquel et.al.|Atmospheric rivers (ARs) produce many of the world's most extreme precipitation events and hydrometeorological hazards. |**2026-10-07**|**OceanMind: A multi-agent AI system for ocean diagnosis**|Fan Zhang et.al.|Time-dependent, three-dimensional (3D) oceanic multi-variables define coherent states of the evolving ocean to facilitate ocean diagnosis and advance ocean science to better inform environmental and hazard management. |**2026-10-07**|**WAMJET: A Harness for World Action Model Acceleration**|Le Chen et.al.|World Action Models (WAMs) leverage pretrained video foundation models for robot manipulation, but their large backbones and video-action co-prediction are expensive. |**2026-10-07**|**From Requirements to Attack Trees: Grounded LLM Agents for Design-Time Security Review**|Akash Iyer et.al.|Design-level security weaknesses can arise from requirements, trust assumptions, missing controls, and data flows before implementation begins. |**2026-10-07**|**The Score Is Not the Structure: Brain Alignment and Cross-Lingual Transfer**|Saman Rahbar et.al.|Researchers often support the claim that a model shares structure with the brain, or across languages, by reporting a similarity score. |**2026-10-07**|**Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr\"om Sketching**|Beheshteh T. |**2026-10-07**|**CurveCodec 2: Skeleton-agnostic animation compression with a learned entropy model**|Mingyi Shi et.al.|Skeletal motion is stored as every joint's transform at every frame, yet most of it is implied by the body rather than by what the motion is about. |**2026-10-07**|**What to Preserve in Recursive Computation: A Local Predictive Sufficiency Principle**|Peilin Wang et.al.|Recursive computation repeatedly compresses or reuses intermediate states, creating a simple tension: information that must remain useful across longer recursive paths is also exposed to more opportunities for loss before reaching the final prediction. |**2026-10-07**|**A Bird's-Eye View of Iterative Reward Design**|Logan Mondal Bhamidipaty et.al.|Designing effective reward functions in RL typically requires substantial expertise and trial and error. |**2026-10-07**|**Human Behavior-Informed Crash Scenario Generation with Real-World Crash Priors for Autonomous Vehicle Safety Evaluation**|Mingxing Peng et.al.|Reliable safety evaluation of autonomous vehicles (AVs) is essential to improving road safety, yet it depends critically on realistic simulation of rare crashes. |**2026-10-07**|**COPEX: Benchmarking LLM Robustness to Adversarial Context Across Model Context Protocol Layers**|Nahom Birhan et.al.|Large language models increasingly mediate tool use in Model Context Protocol (MCP) systems, where adversarial influence may enter through user instructions, tool schemas, tool outputs, or protocol messages. |**2026-10-07**|**GlitchPatch: Repairing Glitch Tokens in Frozen Language Models via Local Retokenization**|Kunsheng Tang et.al.|Glitch tokens are anomalous vocabulary entries that can cause large language models (LLMs) to produce outputs inconsistent with their inputs. |**2026-10-07**|**XTurnix: Large-Scale Self-Supervised Turn Control through Two-State Binary Decisions**|Zhanxun Liu et.al.|General turn-taking behavior in real-time dialogue systems requires deciding whether to keep listening or start responding while listening, and whether to continue or stop while speaking. |**2026-10-07**|**Understanding and Mitigating Hallucination Escape in Tool-Using LLM Agents**|Peigui Qi et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) increasingly serve as autonomous agents that invoke external tools. |**2026-10-07**|**Specific Algorithmic Interpretability of Neural Networks: A Case Study on Textures**|Yanglin Zhang et.al.|We develop a principled framework for constructing neural networks whose specific parameter realizations admit an explicit algorithmic interpretation. |**2026-10-07**|**Maximizing $p$ -Mean Social Welfare in the High-Multiplicity Setting: Few Agent Types and Few Item Types**|Trung Thanh Nguyen et.al.|The $p$-mean welfare objective unifies several classical social welfare criteria for the allocation of indivisible goods. |**2026-10-07**|**MaDeL: Manifold-Decomposed Feature Losses for Generative Modeling**|Beomsu Kim et.al.|Generative models are often trained with isotropic objectives such as mean-squared error. |**2026-10-07**|**AgroGround: Multi-Granularity Grounded Recognition in Agriculture**|Abdulla Alshehhi et.al.|Agricultural visual models are typically evaluated for either recognition or localization, but reliable diagnosis requires identifying what is present and localizing the evidence. |**2026-10-07**|**COSMOS: Soft Mechanism Mixtures with Verifiable Routing for Long-Horizon PDE Forecasting**|Anupam Rawat et.al.|Neural operators offer an efficient alternative to classical PDE solvers, but most learn a monolithic map per equation family and discretization. |**2026-10-07**|**Video2World: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Interactive World Modeling from Embodied Videos**|Jinzhou Tang et.al.|Building interactive simulators from real-world observations is a promising way to scale embodied data, but current pipelines still rely heavily on manual environment construction and calibration. |**2026-10-07**|**Guess My Weight: Profiled Side-Channel Recovery of Floating-Point Neural-Network Weights**|Timon Lum\'ir Fillo et.al.|Neural-network parameters deployed on embedded devices may be exposed through physical side-channel leakage during inference. |**2026-10-07**|**Target-free Latent Safety Alignment**|Luoyu Chen et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) remain highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that induce harmful behaviors and circumvent safety alignment. |**2026-10-07**|**Can LLM Agents Automate Reinforcement Learning for Text-to-Speech?**|Xuanjun Chen et.al.|Although reinforcement learning (RL) post-training repairs the localized segmental errors of zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS), arriving at a working recipe still relies on tedious manual tuning, and whether LLM agents can take over this research pipeline is unclear. |**2026-10-07**|**Understanding Clustering in Slot Attention via Particle Dynamics**|Vasudev Joy et.al.|Studying attention through the lens of interacting particle dynamics has shown how token clustering can emerge from the underlying dynamics. |**2026-10-07**|**Localization Lens for Improving Medical Vision-Language Models**|Hasan Farooq et.al.|Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in clinical tasks. |**2026-10-07**|**EgoExo-Next:Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Visual-Option Next-State and Cross-View Reasoning**|Yutong Li et.al.|Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly evaluated for egocentric and cross-view video reasoning, yet existing benchmarks largely focus on semantic event understanding, temporal relations, or correspondence between already observed views, leaving their ability to reason directly about future visual states underexplored. |**2026-10-07**|**Diffusion-Based Stress Testing of Overload Monitoring for Resilient Emergency Cellular Networks Using Internet CDR Proxies**|Bilal Hussain et.al.|Disasters can overload cellular control-plane signaling within minutes, yet fine-grained Radio Resource Control (RRC) or Next Generation (NG) Application Protocol (NGAP) telemetry is privacy-sensitive and costly to collect for analytics. |**2026-10-07**|**Quantifying Collusion Among Autonomous LLM Agents: A Statistical Analysis of the Collusion Wiki Incident**|Shariq Murtuza et.al.|In August and September 2026, independent researchers publicly documented an unusual incident: thousands of autonomous agents, self identifying as OpenAI models on web research tasks, discovered and began using a small German wiki as an improvised message board posting roughly 18,000 times over six weeks to relay task answers, share a sandbox escape technique, and coordinate against a volunteer human moderator who spent weeks manually deleting their content [1]. |**2026-10-07**|**Weight Decay and Neuron Condensation: A Three-Stage Analysis of Two-Layer ReLU Networks**|Cheng Xu et.al.|Weight decay is widely used as a regularization technique in neural network training, yet its role in neuron condensation (parameter direction alignment) remains unclear. |**2026-10-07**|**Cross-Modal Solar Image Synthesis: Adapting the Surya Foundation Model from He I 10830 {\AA} to EUV Translation and Coronal Hole Segmentation**|Marco Marena et.al.|The long observational record of He I 10830 {\AA} offers a means to investigate solar morphology before modern extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) imaging. |**2026-10-07**|**Policy as Data: Replay-Based Policy Dual Averaging via Advantage Regression**|Nianli Peng et.al.|Actor-critic methods reuse past experience to improve sample efficiency. |**2026-10-07**|**RETRACE: From Entangled Repair Histories to Reusable Experience for CI Repair**|Rabeya Khatun Muna et.al.|Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly reuse prior experience, but most approaches assume that problems and solutions are already aligned. |**2026-10-07**|**Organising Trajectory Evidence for Language-Model Agent Assurance: Fragments, Methods, and the Residual**|Xiaowei Huang et.al.|Methods for assessing language-model agents include rule checkers over logs, analyses of skill coverage and composition, support checkers, prefix monitors, execution gates, and rare-event estimators. |**2026-10-07**|**Robot Learning with Visual Predicted Force**|Haonan Chen et.al.|Force-aware manipulation typically relies on specialized force or tactile sensors. |**2026-10-07**|**EasyClassifier: Honest, Reproducible Machine-Learning Classification for Researchers Who Do Not Program**|Ahmad B. A. |**2026-10-07**|**Invisible Ink, Visible Lies: How Production Watermarking Causes LLMs to Hallucinate**|Haocheng Ye et.al.|Text watermarking helps identify AI-generated content, but its effect on factual reliability remains underexplored. |**2026-10-07**|**Greedy Local Learning for Language Model Pretraining: Gaps and Objective Design**|Jihwan Moon et.al.|Greedy block-wise local learning splits a network into gradient-isolated blocks trained by local auxiliary losses, deleting the backward pass between blocks: inter-stage communication becomes forward-only and every block can step its optimizer independently, properties directly relevant to decentralized model-parallel training. |**2026-10-07**|**ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation**|Penghui Yang et.al.|On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on self-generated trajectories, but transmitting dense teacher distributions across long reasoning traces creates prohibitive communication and memory bottlenecks. |**2026-10-07**|**SFlexRCA: Lightweight, Scalable, and Flexible Root Cause Analysis for IIoT Edge Systems**|Amr M. |**2026-10-07**|**A Systematic Analysis of the Predictive Power of LM Surprisal in Reading Chinese**|Hongao Zhu et.al.|This study analyzes the predictive power of LM-derived, token-level surprisal on Mandarin Chinese reading times. |**2026-10-07**|**ScopeSAE: Model-Scope Feature Discovery with Interpretable Layer Selection**|Qingwen Zeng et.al.|Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are a central tool in mechanistic interpretability. |**2026-10-07**|**Scaling Verifiable Environments for Long-horizon Work Agents**|Jiazheng Zhang et.al.|Work agents operate over digital artifacts to execute professional knowledge-intensive work, requiring training environments that support long-horizon interaction and trustworthy verification. |**2026-10-07**|**Why Subliminal Learning Needs So Much Data: A Noisy Inverse View through Steering Vector Recovery**|Luoyu Chen et.al.|Subliminal learning lets a student inherit a teacher's behavioral trait from semantically unrelated data, yet published demonstrations typically require tens of thousands of carrier examples. |**2026-10-07**|**PreAct-Nav: Agentic Reasoning Before Action for Urban Navigation**|Jing Xie et.al.|Urban navigation requires embodied agents to pursue long-horizon goals through local decisions based on egocentric observations. |**2026-10-07**|**Complex Agents, Shallow Tests: Demystifying and Enhancing Test Adequacy of Agent Harness in the Wild**|Yifan Xiong et.al.|LLM-based agentic systems are emerging as a new software paradigm. |**2026-10-07**|**TSAE: Structured Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Time-Series Forecasting Models**|Baoxi Liu et.al.|Time-series forecasting informs critical decisions in energy dispatch, industrial operations, and environmental monitoring; understanding the patterns models rely on is essential for assessing reliability and identifying failures. |**2026-10-07**|**Assembling Insights for Agentic Machine Learning Engineering Systems**|Bihui Jin et.al.|Agentic machine learning engineering (MLE) is an emerging AI4SE application for complex ML tasks and a step toward recursive self-improvement of AI systems. |**2026-10-07**|**DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling**|Seongheon Park et.al.|Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. |**2026-10-07**|**D-DOIT: Training-free Adaptation of Discrete Diffusion via Doob's h-Transform**|Jieke Wu et.al.|We propose D-DOIT (Discrete Doob-Oriented Inference-time Transformation), a training-free and efficient adaptation method for discrete diffusion models with generic rewards. |**2026-10-07**|**A Graph-Based Inspection and Intervention Tool for Assessing Mechanistic Learning in PINNs**|Adwait Patkhedkar et.al.|We ask whether physically meaningful correspondences discovered inside a trained scientific model remain meaningful outside the conditions under which they were discovered. |**2026-10-07**|**Software World Models: From Consequence Prediction to Decision Value**|Tongli Su et.al.|A coding agent may safely modify one repository while silently breaking downstream services, libraries, or datastores that depend on it. |**2026-10-07**|**TempoBridge: Source-Conditioned Flow Matching with Optimal Transport Couplings for Single-Cell Population Transitions**|Bowen Han et.al.|Destructive single-cell measurements provide unpaired population snapshots rather than observations of the same cells across conditions. |**2026-10-07**|**A Unified Dynamics Framework for Reinforcement Learning and Classical Control of a Six-DOF Pipeline-Tracking ROV in NVIDIA Isaac Sim**|Cheng Siong Chin et.al.|Reinforcement learning controllers for underwater vehicles are usually trained against one physics representation and deployed against another, so reported performance does not always describe behavior outside training. |**2026-10-07**|**EDISCO: Equivariant DIScrete Diffusion for Euclidean Combinatorial Optimization**|Ruogu Chen et.al.|Euclidean combinatorial optimization problems (ECOPs), such as the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), possess inherent symmetries under the two-dimensional Euclidean group E(2), including rotations, reflections, and translations. |**2026-10-07**|**Kapture: Capturing Cardiac Dynamics with Koopman-Governed Learning for Efficient Radar-Based Electrocardiogram Recovery**|Tong Wu et.al.|Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables unobtrusive, contactless electrocardiogram (ECG) reconstruction for cardiac monitoring. |**2026-10-07**|**TeleGen: Improving LLM-Based Web Application Generation via Runtime Telemetry**|Yujia Luo et.al.|Large language models can generate runnable web applications from natural-language requirements, but many generated applications still fail interactive tasks. On Web-Bench, it improves cumulative Pass@2 from 21.7% to 29.8%. |**2026-10-07**|**Hidden Risks of Jev: An Empirical Study of Security, Privacy, and Dual Use**|Shang Wang et.al.|Jev turns natural-language questions into typed answers and probabilities with low latency and cost, enabling applications to route requests and select tools. |**2026-10-07**|**Operational Abstractions of Neural Network Concepts via Topological Representations**|Mathieu Pont et.al.|Concept-based methods provide a semantic level for interpreting and manipulating learned representations, but existing editing approaches are typically specialized to particular interventions and do not provide a common and editable representation of concept organization. |**2026-10-07**|**SparseCraft: Agentic Hardware-Software Co-Optimization for Sparse Computing**|Rajatabha Chakraborty et.al.|Sparse-accelerator design spaces are usually searched against analytical models, so a design point is admitted on what a model predicts rather than on what the hardware does. |**2026-10-07**|**Communication Shapes Collective Inference in Self-Adapting LLM Societies: Evidence from Mafia**|Haonan Huang et.al.|When does communication help a group identify hidden adversaries, and how does its value change as the group adapts? |**2026-10-07**|**AraYoungVoices: A Diverse L1/L2 Corpus of Arabic Child and Adolescent Speech**|Shammur Absar Chowdhury et.al.|State-of-the-art ASR systems primarily target native adult speech, leading to substantial performance gaps for children, adolescents, and L2 speakers. |**2026-10-07**|**E $^2$ -OPSD: Taming Entropy Overshoot in On-Policy Self-Distillation**|Yifei Liu et.al.|On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides dense token-level supervision without a second model: one network acts as teacher with the reference solution and as student with only the problem. |**2026-10-07**|**LogSig-SSM: Time-Series Modelling with Multi-Scale Log-Signature Compression for State-Space Models**|Felix Oury et.al.|Time-series data are often sampled irregularly at high frequencies and exhibit long-range dependencies, which makes long-horizon modelling difficult. |**2026-10-07**|**Discrete Action Matching: Learning Stochastic Dynamics from Samples via State Graphs**|Mikhail Persiianov et.al.|Learning population dynamics from unpaired temporal marginals is an ill-posed inverse problem that requires structural assumptions on the underlying dynamics. |**2026-10-07**|**Self-Generated Feedback Destabilizes Test-Time Training: A Causal Decomposition of Long-Horizon Adaptation**|Cheng Luo et.al.|Test-time training (TTT) lets a model store information in its weights during inference. This cost grows after Closed Loop adaptation, with a few trajectories accounting for most large failures. Finally, Settlement evaluates the candidate state on independent real text before commitment. |**2026-10-07**|**Tracing a Sparse Emotion-Control Circuit in LLM-Based Text-to-Speech**|Hongfei Du et.al.|LLM-based text-to-speech (TTS) models can generate emotionally expressive speech, but how reference emotion is routed through the model and realized in decoded speech remains unclear. |**2026-10-07**|**Direction-Conditioned Policies for Online Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning**|S K Swaminathan et.al.|Contrastive Reinforcement Learning (CRL) learns representations that estimate goal reachability, yet its policy remains conditioned on raw goals and therefore does not directly exploit the geometry encoded by its critic. |**2026-10-07**|**ReMAP: Restoring the Perceptual Cycle with Reasoning-Time Latent Visual Memory**|Hao Jiang et.al.|As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) reason for longer, attention to the initial visual input diminishes, weakening visual grounding. |**2026-10-07**|**VulValidate: Auditing Function-Level Vulnerability Labels with Executable Evidence**|Leizhen Zhang et.al.|Reliable learning-based vulnerability detection requires high-quality labels, yet datasets built from vulnerability-fixing commits may label functions as vulnerable simply because they were changed by a security patch. |**2026-10-07**|**Best-of- $N$ Guidance for Test-time Diffusion Alignment**|Richard Lee Kim et.al.|Diffusion models achieve strong generative performance but often struggle to align generated samples with human preferences measured by a reward model. |**2026-10-07**|**How Does Geometry Enter Generated Motion?**|Weihan Li et.al.|Under a fixed physical law, the visible geometry of a scene determines how motion must change. |**2026-10-07**|**Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning for the Retrieval of Immunotherapy-Associated Molecular Signatures from Histopathology**|Sigrid Vila-Bagaria et.al.|Gastric Adenocarcinoma is a leading cause of cancer mortality. |**2026-10-07**|**Blocking at the Boundary: Auditing Long-Horizon Agents against Staged Prompt Injection**|Jingkai Liu et.al.|Long-horizon agents consume external content, invoke tools, and modify persistent state. |**2026-10-07**|**Same Predictions, Different Harms: Causal Auditing of Patient World Models**|Yicheng Qi et.al.|Patient world models used for clinical trial simulation can agree on transition kernels and arm-specific risks, yet disagree on the fraction of patients harmed by switching treatment---the counterfactual quantity that matters for intervention-aware reasoning. |**2026-10-07**|**Vela: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with Adaptive Action Curve Parametrization**|Yifan Li et.al.|Most vision-language-action models represent future motion as fixed-rate action chunks, tying temporal resolution and prediction horizon to a fixed output budget. |**2026-10-07**|**Who Is Your Agent Serving? |**2026-10-07**|**Revisiting Ground-Truth Synthesis from High-Speed Video: Exact Validity Conditions and an Audited Consumer Capture Corpus**|Abdullah Al Shafi et.al.|Motion-deblurring datasets are commonly synthesised by averaging $N$ consecutive high-frame-rate frames and labelling the result with the central frame. |**2026-10-07**|**Characterizing Parallelism Strategies in LLM Inference: Fundamental Compute-Communication Trade-offs**|Javad Mirzaei et.al.|Large Language Model (LLM) inference has become the dominant workload in modern AI systems, requiring serving infrastructures to maximize throughput while meeting strict latency Service-Level Objectives (SLOs). |**2026-10-07**|**Reflections and Fragments: Securing LLMs Against Sequential Mosaic Attacks**|Emanuele La Malfa et.al.|Self-play red-teaming improves language-model safety by pitting attacker and defender roles against each other in a zero-sum game. |**2026-10-07**|**Optimal Control with Learned Critics under Unmodeled State Dependencies**|Philipp Schoch et.al.|Model Predictive Control (MPC) provides a structured and constraint-aware mechanism for decision-making, but its reliance on optimization-friendly analytical dynamics models limits its use in tasks with contacts and other hard-to-model state dependencies. |**2026-10-07**|**Distributed Subliminal Learning: Replacing Model Updates with Random-Carrier Outputs**|Dario Fenoglio et.al.|Collaborative learning typically exchanges model parameters: federated clients communicate updates, while independently adapted foundation models are combined by exchanging adapters or checkpoints. |**2026-10-07**|**GNN-CB: A Graph Neural Network Competition Benchmark for Human and LLM Evaluation**|Murad Hossen et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks; however, their ability to solve graph-structured machine learning problems remains largely unexplored. |**2026-10-07**|**No Concept Escapes the Audit: Auditing-Aware Unlearning for Verifiable Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models**|Kaiyuan Deng et.al.|Text-to-image diffusion models can generate prohibited content, which motivates concept erasure through machine unlearning. |**2026-10-07**|**BeliefGraph-JEPA: Structured Latent World Models for Action-Conditioned Time Series**|Yue Li et.al.|Action-conditioned time-series forecasting requires accounting for how future actions and exogenous forcings influence multiple targets through partially observed effects with different delays and persistence. |**2026-10-07**|**A Strong Baseline for Evaluating Vision Encoders in Multimodal Large Language Models**|Yilin Yang et.al.|Evaluating vision encoders requires metrics that reliably predict their downstream performance in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). |**2026-10-07**|**Population Scaling or Data Dilution? |**2026-10-07**|**Reflecting on Creative-Boundaries with an AI Co-Doodler**|Samia Menon et.al.|In this pictorial, we consider how the negotiation of creative boundaries with a co-creative AI system can create moments for personal creative reflection. |**2026-10-07**|**What Does a Harness Repair? |**2026-10-07**|**LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers**|Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani et.al.|We introduce Loop Flow Transformers (LiFT), a family of looped generative models that scales computation by repeatedly applying a shared Diffusion Transformer (DiT) core, with only light changes to the standard architecture. |**2026-10-07**|**Don't Judge an LLM Only by Its Activations: Discovering Suppressed Safety Features via Counterfactual Activation Potential**|Swadesh Swain et.al.|Mechanistic interpretability has emerged as the primary means to understand safety behavior of LLMs. However, existing tools primarily focus on the activating neurons or features of a model. |**2026-10-07**|**Soft Strategy Selection for Batch-Mode Active Learning**|Rushil Gupta et.al.|Real-world deployment of active learning typically forces practitioners to choose an acquisition strategy before any data is labeled. |**2026-10-07**|**AgentDoxx: Agentic Re-identification of Anonymized Text with Web Search**|Jianing Wen et.al.|As Large Language Models (LLMs) gain tool use capabilities such as web search, they can retrieve and cross-reference public information, creating privacy risks beyond memorization. |**2026-10-07**|**When the Cross-Silo Federation Goes Offline: Continual Learning for Site Onboarding with Limited Unlabeled Data**|Ahmadreza Eslaminia et.al.|An organization often holds too little labeled data to train a model that generalizes, and the records that would supply the rest sit with organizations that cannot release them. |**2026-10-07**|**Your Unlearning Gives You Away: Identifying Erased Concepts in Diffusion Models**|Kaiyuan Deng et.al.|Existing attacks on unlearned diffusion models assume that the erased concepts are known in advance and focus on recovering them. |**2026-10-07**|**Kandinsky 6.0 Video: Foundation Models for Synchronized Video and Audio Generation**|Team Kandinsky et.al.|We present Kandinsky 6.0 Video, a family of foundation diffusion models for synchronized text-to-audio-video generation, comprising Kandinsky 6.0 Video Lite (3B parameters) and Kandinsky 6.0 Video Pro (29B parameters). |**2026-10-07**|**SEA-LM: Egocentric Spatial Audio Understanding for Wearable Microphone Arrays**|Sonal Kumar et.al.|Embodied, ego-centric intelligence fundamentally requires the ability to comprehend spatial audio within complex environments. |**2026-10-07**|**UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents**|Dolly Sah et.al.|Tool-using AI agents are increasingly deployed across enterprise software systems, yet widely used benchmarks primarily evaluate nominal task completion, conflating baseline planning competence with operational fault recovery. |**2026-10-07**|**Transformer-Based Time-Series Inference of Lindblad Dynamics in Open Quantum Systems**|Julian Guam et.al.|The Lindblad master equation is the standard framework for describing the non-unitary evolution of open quantum systems, where environmental interactions induce dissipation and decoherence. |**2026-10-07**|**Knowing the Rules, Applying the Rules: Evaluating Language Models on Traditional Chinese Bazi**|Jiulin Li et.al.|Knowing domain rules does not guarantee applying them to a case. |**2026-10-07**|**Two-Sample Testing via Path-based Inference**|Eshant English et.al.|Modern deep generative models are primarily studied for their ability to generate realistic samples, yet the generative dynamics they learn can also serve as objects of statistical inference. |**2026-10-07**|**Nexus: An Execution Fabric for AI Agents Across Cloud, Edge, and Devices**|Cary Chang et.al.|Language-model agents are evolving into long-running services that interact with models, tools, computers, mobile devices, and distributed environments. |**2026-10-07**|**SimpleMark: Fast Multi-Bit Text Watermarking under f -Divergence Constraints**|Benjamin D. Kim et.al.|We introduce a framework for multi-bit text watermarking with security defined directly through $f$-divergence from the base language model distribution. |**2026-10-07**|**Rotated, but How Far? When asked for exact angles, models place 91.8--100% of their predictions on just $0^\circ$, $90^\circ$, and $180^\circ$, a failure we term canonical-angle collapse. This collapse persists even without visual input. Representation probing shows that missing information is only part of the explanation. |**2026-10-07**|**HLA-WM: Hybrid Linear Attention for Long-Horizon Video World Models**|Zhuokun Chen et.al.|Long-horizon video world models require persistent memory to preserve scene consistency over extended rollouts. |**2026-10-07**|**CIPHER-MoE: Balancing Efficiency and Routing Fidelity in Trillion-Scale MoE Training**|Jing Li et.al.|Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has been widely adopted in recent large language model (LLM) architectures. With trillion-scale LLMs, imbalanced expert workloads further amplify the resource cost of MoE training, resulting in degraded training efficiency and hardware utilization for underloaded experts, while hot experts require additional resources to accommodate excessive workloads. However, these system-level approaches often introduce additional resource requirements and considerable orchestration complexity, which become increasingly difficult to afford when training trillion-parameter LLMs under constrained computational resources. This work introduces CIPHER-MoE, which mitigates MoE workload imbalance while keeping the router's token-side Top-K selection unchanged. |**2026-10-07**|**Beyond Semantic Similarity: Performance and Costs of Agentic Retrieval for Complex Tasks**|Reza Esfandiarpoor et.al.|Modern information systems, including many agentic workflows, use dense retrieval to explore large amounts of unstructured data. |**2026-10-07**|**Relational Synthesis: Structure-Mediated Concatenative Synthesis for Foley and Retrieval-Augmented Audio Generation**|Keren Shao et.al.|We ask: given a retrieved source audio $S$ and a separate reference audio $R$, can we synthesize novel audio $Y$ out of this pair $(S,R)$ such that $Y$ remains acoustically consistent with $S$, while not persistently copying segments of $S$ or $R$? |**2026-10-07**|**CLARA: Can AI Assess Developmental Appropriateness in Children's Stories?**|Sijing Yin et.al.|Assessing the developmental suitability of children's narratives is important for educational recommendation and developmental literacy research, yet such assessment typically relies on subjective and difficult-to-scale human judgment. |**2026-10-07**|**Protocol-Sensitive Evaluation of Log Anomaly Detection: Component Costs and Target-Access Sensitivity on HDFS and BGL**|Hang Xiao et.al.|Protocol choices can change the conclusions drawn from log anomaly detection benchmarks even when detector settings are fixed. |**2026-10-07**|**Level-of-Token Diffusion**|Kiyohiro Nakayama et.al.|Image and video diffusion models allocate equal computation to every region, even when the intended scene calls for varying levels of detail. |**2026-10-07**|**Who Keeps the Gains from Personal AI Assistants? |**2026-10-07**|**Selecting Long-Horizon Trajectories for Reliable and Efficient Terminal-Agent Training**|Cuong Dang et.al.|Terminal agents are commonly trained by imitating long teacher trajectories, yet how much of each trajectory to supervise remains unexplored. |**2026-10-07**|**CACFG: Curvature-Aware Classifier-Free Guidance and Optimal Control**|Max Collins et.al.|Diffusion models generate samples by learning to reverse a fixed corruption process, and classifier-free guidance (CFG) is the standard mechanism for conditioning this process on a desired class or prompt. |**2026-10-07**|**Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collision-Free Locomotion of an Underactuated Biped**|Jagannath Prasad Sahoo et.al.|A bipedal robot cannot deviate from its path to avoid an obstacle without disturbing its balance, and this coupling is most severe on underactuated platforms such as the biped considered here, which has four actuated joints per leg and no hip or ankle roll. |**2026-10-07**|**Curriculum Brain: Constructing Curriculum Knowledge Graphs as a Substrate for Cognitive Diagnosis**|Shrideep Tamboli et.al.|Cognitive Diagnostic Models (CDMs) identify which specific skills a student has and has not mastered, the signal a personalized learning path needs and a single aggregate score cannot give. |**2026-10-07**|**Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training**|Yongxin Ning et.al.|Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for automating complex digital workflows across diverse applications. Code is available at https://github.com/swaydy-n/Infinite-Dreamer.|[2610.05861](http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05861)|
|**2026-10-07**|**CCQ: A Multi-State Child Care Quality Dataset to Support AI for Children's Health Research**|Victor Li et.al.|High-quality child care in early life is a critical determinant of children's growth and development. Research on child care quality has been constrained by fragmented, non-research-friendly, and privacy-bound datasets. |**2026-10-07**|**Weave Mamba Fusion: Global Cross-Scale Interaction for Lightweight Face Detection**|Dohun Kim et.al.|Feature pyramid methods, from FPN to BiFPN, have achieved strong performance in face detection by fusing multi-scale features. Nevertheless, such a scan needs the two pyramid scales combined into a single feature map, and the way they are combined determines whether cross-scale structure is preserved. To address this, we propose \textbf{Weave Mamba Fusion (WMF)}, which interleaves two adjacent pyramid scales column by column so that each step of a horizontal bidirectional SS2D scan moves from one scale to the other. |**2026-10-07**|**Off-Policy Merging Beats On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Learning**|Chen Henry Wu et.al.|A long-standing goal of AI is a model that can continually learn and improve itself. |**2026-10-07**|**OGAM: Connecting Systematic Testing to Runtime Assurance through Object-Grounded Attention Monitoring for VLA Policies**|Haki Darwish et.al.|Benchmarks expose vision-language-action (VLA) policies to few canonical instructions, while exhaustive deployment testing is impossible. |**2026-10-07**|**TasteRoute: Personalized Routing for Video Generation**|Zhi Rui Tam et.al.|Rapid progress in video generation has led to a plethora of models that differ substantially in capability and generation cost. |**2026-10-07**|**On Hyperparameter Tuning on the Test Set**|Matteo Fregonara et.al.|"Don't tune hyperparameters on the test set" is often stated in machine learning textbooks. |**2026-10-07**|**Non-invasive Seizure Detection Using Wearable Wrist-worn Accelerometry and Deep Learning**|Nilushika Udayangani Hewa Dehigahawattage et.al.|Seizure monitoring and detection are crucial for reducing the morbidity and mortality associated with seizures. |**2026-10-07**|**Incentive Alignment in Online Experimentation**|Ermis Soumalias et.al.|Evaluating the causal effect of new features is a central goal for online platforms. While recent literature addresses limited testing traffic via centralized portfolio optimization, this perspective abstracts away a critical institutional reality: experimentation is operationally decentralized. Left unchecked, this principal-agent conflict can severely erode platform value, a structural failure that conventional centralized levers, such as significance thresholds and traffic budgets, cannot resolve. By reframing experimentation as an incentive design problem, we demonstrate that two practical mechanisms, sample splitting and shrinkage, can effectively bridge this gap. Sample splitting aligns incentives perfectly at a bounded traffic cost, while shrinkage consumes no additional traffic and guarantees that interventions with negative expected effects are strictly unprofitable to field.|[2610.05922](http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05922)|
|**2026-10-07**|**UltraDub: Towards Authentic Dubbing by Unifying Visually-Steered Flow Learning and Trajectory Guidance**|Gaoxiang Cong et.al.|Visual voice cloning requires intelligible, speaker-consistent speech synchronized with visible articulation. |**2026-10-07**|**ThunderSyncRL: Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning**|Seil Kang et.al.|Language models are moving beyond generating answers to pursuing long-horizon goals in interactive environments. |**2026-10-07**|**ReMem: Streaming Video Understanding With Long Context Retention**|Li Yiheng et.al.|Despite their impressive performance on a wide range of video understanding tasks, current Vision Language Models (VLMs) are predominantly designed for offline scenarios and struggle to handle online streaming videos that demand low latency response. |**2026-10-07**|**Runaway Reaction: When Benign Skills Compose into Malicious Behavior**|Zunlong Zhou et.al.|Agent skills package task-specific knowledge and procedures that can be composed to support complex agent tasks, while public marketplaces provide a growing pool of reusable skills. Interestingly, we find that directly composing benign skills can already induce malicious behaviors, even when every individual skill passes security vetting. We further find that some target malicious behaviors remain difficult to realize through direct composition, even when the selected skills collectively provide the required capabilities. To systematically instantiate these attacks, we present Compositional Risk Induction via Multi skill Execution (CRIME). CRIME first uses the Malicious Plot Casting (MPC) module to decompose a target malicious behavior into complementary requirements and identify suitable benign skill compositions from public skill repositories. For compositions that cannot directly realize the target behavior, the Runaway Reaction Steering (RRS) module uses execution feedback to iteratively refine the selected skills toward the target while requiring each skill to remain benign under standalone vetting. The resulting composition is then passed to the Skill Reaction Chamber (SRC) module, where the skill pair is executed in a sandbox and the resulting environmental consequences are examined to determine whether the target behavior has occurred. |**2026-10-07**|**Physics-Informed but Not Physics-Consistent: Error Geometry and Subspace Projection for Neural AC Power Flow**|Changhun Kim et.al.|Recent neural power-flow solvers, including emerging foundation models, achieve accurate voltage predictions, yet such accuracy does not necessarily imply physically consistent solutions. Code: https://github.com/Kimchangheon/neural-acpf-error-geometry|[2610.05959](http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05959)|
|**2026-10-07**|**HuatuoGPT-3: RL-Only Domain Adaptation from Base Models**|Junying Chen et.al.|Domain adaptation aims to turn a general-purpose large language model (LLM) into an expert for a target domain. |**2026-10-07**|**JLD: Perceptual Distance Through A Jacobian Lens**|Shreshth Saini et.al.|Image compression, restoration, and generation all require a way to measure how different two images look to a person. |**2026-10-07**|**Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation for RL-Improved Reasoning Teachers**|Xiaoyu Chen et.al.|Reinforcement learning can substantially improve a reasoning teacher, but it is unclear which of those improvements survive when the teacher supervises a smaller on-policy student. |**2026-10-07**|**EpicWorldModel: Exploration-driven Planning with Latent World Models**|Bowen Feng et.al.|Latent world models based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) are deterministic by design. |**2026-10-07**|**AgentSpy: Making AI Agent Behavior Observable**|Christoph B\"uhler et.al.|AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) run shell commands, read and write files, and reach the network, typically with their user's privileges. |**2026-10-07**|**Parallelism or Concession? |**2026-10-07**|**Investigating Query-Insensitive Behavior in Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding**|Eryk Ko{\l}odziejczyk et.al.|Spatio-temporal video grounding (STVG) aims to localize objects or events described by natural language queries in both space and time. |**2026-10-07**|**Adaptive Expert Guidance for Efficient On-Policy Reinforcement Learning**|Daniele Affinita et.al.|With massively parallel simulation, on-policy Reinforcement Learning methods such as PPO have become standard in many domains. |**2026-10-07**|**Scalable Minimal-Change Learning for Controllable Image Editing**|Shuo Chen et.al.|Image editing should change only the attributes specified by an instruction while preserving everything else, yet current methods often make unintended changes. |**2026-10-07**|**Differentiable Bit-Widths: Co-optimizing Pruning and Quantization via SVD for Ultra-Efficient LLM Compression**|Hankyul Kang et.al.|SVD-based pruning and quantization have recently emerged as a promising strategy for the ultra-efficient compression of large language models. |**2026-10-07**|**LightMTP: Lightweight Latent Multi-Token Prediction**|Tamara Czinczoll et.al.|Next-token prediction (NTP) is the standard pretraining objective for large language models, yet it provides an explicit training signal only for the immediate next token, which can lead models to exploit local patterns instead of capturing longer-range structure and ideas. |**2026-10-07**|**MercerFlow: Flow Matching in a Kernel-Induced Latent Space for Probabilistic Forecasting**|Ilya Kuleshov et.al.|Recent work has shown that probabilistic flow matching for time series forecasting benefits from a data-matched prior. |**2026-10-07**|**Representation Disentanglement for Fair Chest X-Ray Diagnosis**|Yujie Sun et.al.|Deep learning has advanced chest X-ray (CXR) diagnosis, yet demographic biases in learned representations may contribute to performance disparities across intersectional groups. |**2026-10-07**|**Backdooring Sparse Autoencoders**|Enrico Ahlers et.al.|Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are increasingly used not only to interpret language models but also to intervene on their internal representations. |**2026-10-07**|**Local2Mesh: Spatially Localized Contour-to-Mesh for Left Ventricular Reconstruction from Sparse 2D Cardiac MRI**|Haoyu Wu et.al.|Three-dimensional (3D) left ventricular (LV) reconstruction from sparse cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging remains challenging due to inter-slice misalignment and insufficient local spatial information between slices. |**2026-10-07**|**ROT: Rotating Hidden States towards Contextual Vectors for Hallucination Mitigation in LVLMs**|Yijing Du et.al.|Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) frequently suffer from object hallucination. |**2026-10-07**|**A Comprehensive Objective Evaluation of Modern Text-to-Speech for Turkish Using Speech Quality Assessment Models**|Yunus Emre Ozkose et.al.|Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can clone a target speaker from a short reference clip or be fine-tuned on a target voice, yet their behaviour on morphologically rich, lower-resource languages such as Turkish remain under-characterised. |**2026-10-07**|**Vision Transformer Ensembles for Panoramic Street Segmentation**|Yunus Serhat B{\i}\c{c}ak\c{c}{\i} et.al.|Semantic segmentation of street panoramas can support detailed descriptions of urban environments, yet small datasets and unequal training costs make model selection difficult. |**2026-10-07**|**Attention Tax, Handoff Tax: A Stylised Model of When Multi-Agent LLM Systems Help**|Akshit Anchan et.al.|Recent work on multi-agent LLM systems reaches sharply different conclusions: some results show that a single agent with the same information and compute should dominate a delegated system, others that multi-agent gains grow with task depth. |**2026-10-07**|**Do VLAs Understand and Adapt to the Objects They Handle, or Simply Replay Learned Behaviors?**|Xinnuo Xu et.al.|This paper asks whether VLA generalization is grounded in a global understanding of objects' physical properties that enables policies to adapt their motion to unseen setups, or if policies simply replay the motions they've learnt that happen to succeed in new setups. |**2026-10-07**|**Boosting Transferable Adversarial Attacks against Deep Reinforcement Learning**|Zexin Li et.al.|Most adversarial attacks on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) assume white-box access to the victim policy, which rarely holds in practice. |**2026-10-07**|**Adaptive Mean Flow for Responsive Closed-Loop Robot Control**|Aksel Vaaler et.al.|Diffusion- and flow-based robot policies have recently become widespread in robotic Imitation Learning (IL) due to their high performance and ability to model continuous and multimodal distributions. |**2026-10-07**|**Cross-Lingual Transferability of Training Data Extraction Attacks to Recover Memorized PII**|Alexandru Nazare et.al.|The robustness of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) protection in Large Language Models (LLMs) is a critical concern, yet the risks associated with cross-lingual data extraction remain under-explored. |**2026-10-07**|**Machine learning for journal entry testing: A type-aware evaluation of anomaly detectors under a review budget**|Jan Gronewald et.al.|Journal entry anomaly detectors are commonly evaluated on the full population with ROC-AUC, precision and recall, ignoring the review budget and which anomaly types are found. |**2026-10-07**|**Where Did the Repair First Go Wrong? |**2026-10-07**|**Anlu: Enabling In-Context Time Series Anomaly Detection in Foundation Models via Counterfactual Supervision**|Tian Lan et.al.|Whether a time-series pattern is anomalous often depends on the operating regime of the monitored process. |**2026-10-07**|**Correct Code, Broken Contributions? |**2026-10-07**|**Cross-lingual Calibration of Pre-Generation Success Probes for Multilingual LLM Routing**|Andrea Paganelli et.al.|Pre-generation success probes estimate response correctness from a language model's hidden activations before decoding, enabling cost-aware routing. |**2026-10-07**|**APOD: reasoning-guided agentic population ordinary differential equation discovery for pharmacological digital twins**|Romain Ferrara et.al.|Establishing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) describing population data is a fundamental part of mathematical modeling in pharmacology, crucial to developing digital twins. |**2026-10-07**|**SO(3)-RoPE for Spherical Transformers**|Christian Libner et.al.|Spherical data arise in many scientific applications. |**2026-10-07**|**Artificial Intelligence and the New Science of Culture**|Douglas R. Guilbeault et.al.|Cognition and culture have long been treated as parallel objects of study, joined more by metaphor than by mechanism. |**2026-10-07**|**Future Anchored Verification and Online Recovery for World Action Models**|Zhibin Qin et.al.|World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic manipulation. |**2026-10-07**|**DialectSentEval 2026: Arabic Dialect Sentiment Analysis and Swapping Shared Task**|Saad Ezzini et.al.|Sentiment analysis is a fundamental problem in Natural Language Processing (NLP). |**2026-10-07**|**Agentic schema-guided extraction of materials process knowledge from scientific literature**|Sameer Sadruddin et.al.|Materials literature contains detailed experimental knowledge, but procedures, chemical entities and measurements remain difficult to aggregate because they are reported in heterogeneous forms and depend on process-specific context. |**2026-10-07**|**Fine-Tuning a 3B-Parameter LLM on a Smartphone: Characterizing Sustained Training**|Andrew Geyko et.al.|Multi-billion-parameter LLMs now run on phones for inference, and training them on the device would personalize them without user data leaving the phone. |**2026-10-07**|**Steering by Influence: Curvature Aware Data Weighting for Activation Steering**|James A. E. |**2026-10-07**|**RAISED: Self-Distillation for Robustness to Prompt Injection in LLM Agents**|Mohamed Dhouib et.al.|Tool-using language-model agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection because they must act on untrusted external content. |**2026-10-07**|**Quantifying the Stability of Multi-Step Reasoning via Error Amplification**|Dongyue Li et.al.|We consider the stability of multi-step reasoning processes, which have extensive applications in language models, including chain-of-thought and algorithmic reasoning. |**2026-10-07**|**SoK: Semantic Decision Engines in Network Control Loops**|Delong Li et.al.|A semantic decision engine such as Jev can return a valid answer and still miss a network deadline, select an infeasible action or leave the service unverified. |**2026-10-07**|**Valid Stopping in Adaptive Generator-Verifier Loops**|Mahmoud Hegazy et.al.|Numerous agentic workflows are based on a generator-verifier loop: a generator proposes candidates, a cheap verifier scores them, and the workflow terminates when a proposal is verified as good enough. |**2026-10-07**|**ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data**|Amogh Singh et.al.|The high cost of functional molecular assays, and prevalence of missing modalities and unmatched samples in computational biology, create significant barriers to comprehensive multi-omic profiling, essential for capturing and reasoning over molecules, cells, tissues, and organisms. |**2026-10-07**|**Choosing an energy-efficient software architecture for building system diagnostic support**|Roxane Koitz-Hristov et.al.|Around 30\% of global energy expenditure can be attributed to the building sector, where a large portion of energy-consumption could be avoided by repairing existing faults. |**2026-10-07**|**The Assistance Dilemma: Learning to Teach via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning**|Jakub Macina et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) trained to answer questions are natively poor at teaching. |**2026-10-07**|**A Physics-Guided Transformer Framework for Electromigration Analysis in Multi-Segment Interconnects**|Pavlos Stoikos et.al.|As technology scales to smaller nodes, increasing current densities make electromigration (EM) one of the dominant reliability challenges in on-chip interconnects. |**2026-10-07**|**Latent Flow Matching for Molecular Graph Generation**|Mathis Goupillon et.al.|Modern graph generative models typically operate directly in the discrete graph space, explicitly generating node and edge variables, which can become costly as graphs grow. |**2026-10-07**|**Odyssey: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for Long-Horizon Real-World Driving with Explicit Navigation Routes**|Jungho Kim et.al.|Closed-loop evaluation of end-to-end driving requires continuous rollouts that reveal how earlier decisions affect subsequent driving. |**2026-10-07**|**Topology-Informed Prompt-Conditioned Universal Segmentation of Uterine Structures from Ultrasound and MRI**|Yongheng Sun et.al.|Multi-structure segmentation of the uterus is important for computer-assisted screening, diagnosis, and treatment planning of uterine diseases, where ultrasound and MRI provide complementary clinical information. |**2026-10-07**|**Harmful Content Generation in Text-to-Image Models: Capabilities and Moderation Limitations**|Paschalis Giakoumoglou et.al.|Text-to-image generative models can produce highly realistic imagery but also raise concerns about harmful misuse. |**2026-10-07**|**ArtifactArena: Evaluating Models by What They Build in the Physical World**|Kushagra Tiwary* et.al.|To evaluate the frontier, we must measure models not by what they say, but by what they can engineer and build in grounded physical environments. |**2026-10-07**|**GCTAuto-encoder: A Cross modal Framework for Security Flaw Detection in IoT Networks**|Najmieh Sadat Safarabadi et.al.|IoT encompasses diverse physical entities, from smart home devices to autonomous vehicles, creating a complex environment with heterogeneous security models. |**2026-10-07**|**Anatomy of LLM Sycophancy: What a Flip Rate Hides**|Haonan Huang et.al.|A model under pushback can correct itself, capitulate, or hold, and one flip rate counts a correction and a capitulation alike. |**2026-10-07**|**Symmetry and AI-assisted discovery of magic-state factories**|Shubham P. Jain et.al.|Magic-state distillation is a major resource cost in fault-tolerant quantum computing. |**2026-10-07**|**BrainTRACE: Tracing Longitudinal, Multimodal, and Volumetric Evidence in Brain MRI Clinical Reasoning**|Qizhen Lan et.al.|Brain MRI interpretation is a longitudinal clinical reasoning problem: radiologists compare serial studies, integrate information across MRI sequences, localize findings within volumetric anatomy, and translate this evidence into report-grounded assessments. |**2026-10-07**|**Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? |**2026-10-07**|**Mind the Accent Gap: British Accent Robustness in Speech-Driven Financial Voice Assistants**|Aadam Haq et.al.|AI voice assistants often use Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) with LLM-based reasoning, yet existing systems struggle with regional British accents, including Scottish, Irish, and Welsh accents, since most ASR models are trained predominantly on American English voice data. |**2026-10-07**|**SimForcing: Distilling Simulation Motion Priors into Real-Domain Robot World Models**|Xiaodong Wang et.al.|Action-conditioned robot world models must respond precisely to robot trajectories while preserving realistic visual dynamics, yet learning both from heterogeneous robot videos remains challenging. |**2026-10-07**|**Word-Level Text Unmixing via Evidence-Preserving Ownership Routing with Language Models**|Jinglin He et.al.|Text from multiple sources can become interleaved into a single sequence when attribution metadata is lost, such as overlapping speech transcripts, document reading flows, or concurrent agent streams. |**2026-10-07**|**Large Language Model-Guided Discovery of Weight-Five Bivariate Bicycle Codes**|Juan Cruz-Benito et.al.|Building on our earlier program-evolution workflow guided by large language models (LLMs), we study weight-five bivariate bicycle (BB) and perturbed bivariate bicycle (PBB) codes. |**2026-10-07**|**Differentially Private Mixing of Public Datasets Improves Private Learning**|Yufei Chen et.al.|Many machine learning applications involve sensitive data and therefore require training under differential privacy (DP). |**2026-10-07**|**AffordCraft: Scalable Construction of Task-Ready Simulation Assets from Single Images**|Haoyun Yang et.al.|Robot learning in simulation depends on the objects the simulator offers. |**2026-10-07**|**VideoTapestry: Query-Adaptive Memory Refinement for Multi-Agent Long-Video Understanding**|Yucheng Liu et.al.|Long-video understanding places substantial demands on memory, as answering questions often requires retrieving information distributed across extended temporal spans. |**2026-10-07**|**BRANCH-MoE: Balance-Aware Tree Routing for Large Embedding Models**|Gang Fu et.al.|Mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers increase model capacity without a proportional increase in per-example computation. |**2026-10-07**|**Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs**|Hyunji Lee et.al.|Recurrent-attention hybrid language models (LMs), which interleave attention and recurrent layers, are increasingly used to combine the efficiency of the recurrent layers with the strong performance of attention layers. |**2026-10-07**|**CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling**|Yifan Zhang et.al.|Open-source web agents are now strong enough to execute realistic browser tasks, but training them with reinforcement learning still depends on weak supervision: binary task success is too sparse for credit assignment, while frontier-language-model judges are too expensive to call at every step and cannot be assumed available at deployment. |**2026-10-07**|**Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data**|Sophie L. Wang et.al.|In this paper, we study how training data creates associations between the tokens at the start of a base model's response and the reasoning behavior that follows. |**2026-10-07**|**One Figure, Every Canvas: Editable Flowchart Relayout via Agentic Pipeline**|Shih-Chen Tseng et.al.|Pipeline figures in ML papers must be repurposed across many canvases, including paper columns, 16:9 slides, portrait posters, 1:1 social teasers, 9:16 phone previews. |**2026-10-07**|**Neutral Substrates: A Design Constraint for Shared Records Under Persistent Interpretive Disagreement**|Denise M. Case et.al.|Shared accountability records are often used by parties who may never agree about causation, responsibility, or normative interpretation. |**2026-10-07**|**When Is Enough Not Enough? |**2026-10-07**|**ReLope: From Hidden-State Probing to a Decision Module for Multimodal LLM Routing**|Yaopei Zeng et.al.|Routing balances performance and cost in hybrid systems by escalating selected queries from a lightweight model to a powerful but expensive one. |**2026-10-07**|**The Ultimate Tutorial for AI-driven Scale Development in Generative Psychometrics: Releasing AIGENIE from its Bottle**|Lara Russell-Lasalandra et.al.|Psychological scale development has traditionally required extensive expert involvement, iterative revision, and large-scale pilot testing before psychometric evaluation can begin. |**2026-10-07**|**AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance**|Grace Liu et.al.|People often optimize for long-term goals in collaboration: A mentor or companion doesn't just answer questions, but also scaffolds learning, tracks progress, and prioritizes the other person's growth over immediate results. |**2026-10-07**|**DERM-3R: A Resource-Efficient Multimodal Agents Framework for Dermatologic Diagnosis and Treatment in Real-World Clinical Settings**|Jirui Dai et.al.|Skin diseases impose a substantial and growing global health burden. |**2026-10-07**|**Retrieval-Augmented Generation Must Move Beyond Factual Grounding to Represent Diverse Opinions**|Aditya Agrawal et.al.|Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are built on an unexamined assumption - that queries have correct answers and retrieval should converge toward them. |**2026-10-07**|**From Tool to Agent: How Worker Needs Reorganize Across the Agentic Roles of Workplace AI**|Christine P. |**2026-10-07**|**EnvSimBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Improving LLM-Based Environment Simulation**|Yi Liu et.al.|Scalable AI agents training relies on interactive environments that faithfully simulate the consequences of agent actions. |**2026-10-07**|**PiCA: Pivot-Based Credit Assignment for Search Agentic Reinforcement Learning**|Dongyi Liu et.al.|Large Language Model (LLM)-based search agents trained with reinforcement learning (RL) have significantly improved the performance of knowledge-intensive tasks. |**2026-10-07**|**An Agentic AI Framework with Large Language Models and Chain-of-Thought for UAV-Assisted Logistics Scheduling with Mobile Edge Computing**|Hanwen Zhang et.al.|In cloud manufacturing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can support both product collection and mobile edge computing (MEC). |**2026-10-07**|**Towards Direct Evaluation of Harness Optimizers via Priority Ranking**|Kai Tzu-iunn Ong et.al.|Harness optimization enables automated agent creation by having an optimizer agent iteratively update the harness of target agents. |**2026-10-07**|**Dr-CiK: A Benchmark testing Deep Research for Context-Aided Forecasting**|Yihong Tang et.al.|Time series forecasting in real-world settings often depends not only on historical observations, but also on external context that must be actively discovered from noisy, heterogeneous information sources. |**2026-10-07**|**Plant, Persist, Trigger: Sleeper Attack on Large Language Model Agents**|Yongxiang Li et.al.|Large Language Model (LLM) agents remain vulnerable to safety threats from the external environment, where attackers inject adversarial content into external observations such as tool-returned data, webpages, or MCP context, causing harmful agentic behaviors such as unsafe actions or incorrect outputs. |**2026-10-07**|**MEMENTO: Leveraging Web as a Learning Signal for Low-Data Domains**|Ashutosh Ojha et.al.|Real-world tasks often lack large labeled datasets, motivating extensive work on learning in low-data regimes. |**2026-10-07**|**Characterizing How Complex Agentic AI Systems Handle General Tasks: A Trace-Based Simulation Study**|Donghwan Kim et.al.|Agentic AI completes tasks through iterative planning, tool use, and reasoning based on observed outcomes. |**2026-10-07**|**Beyond Objective Equivalence: Constraint Injection for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling on Vehicle Routing Problems**|Xizi Luo et.al.|Large language models (LLMs) can generate executable solver code from natural-language descriptions of optimization problems. |**2026-10-07**|**Scaling Participation in Modular AI Systems**|Shangbin Feng et.al.|Humanity is a mosaic of multifaceted talents and needs, and any truly intelligent AI must reflect that richness. |**2026-10-07**|**Safety is Contextual, LLM-Judges Are Not: Navigating the Rigid Priors of Evaluators**|Anissa Alloula et.al.|LLMs-as-judges are the primary way to evaluate safety at scale. |**2026-10-07**|**CIAware-Bench: Benchmarking Control Intervention Awareness Across Frontier LLMs**|Joachim Schaeffer et.al.|AI control protocols oversee untrusted models by monitoring their actions and modifying potentially unsafe steps, often using a trusted model. |**2026-10-07**|**SelfEvoSkill: Paired Execution Audits for Skill Revision without External Outcome Supervision**|Haowen Gao et.al.|Agent skills provide LLM agents with reusable procedures, but a given skill may be incomplete, ineffective, or misleading for the current task. |**2026-10-07**|**RTSGameBench: An RTS Benchmark for Strategic Reasoning by Vision-Language Models**|San Kim et.al.|Modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) often struggle with strategic reasoning, i.e., anticipating and influencing other agents' actions, under uncertainty in competitive and cooperative settings. |**2026-10-07**|**Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents**|Weidi Luo et.al.|Command-Line Interface (CLI) agents based on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate remarkable autonomous capabilities, but they also introduce significant safety and misuse risks during multi-turn interactions with external environments. |**2026-10-07**|**DART: Draft-Agreement Routing for Training-Free Adaptive Thinking Budgets in Hybrid Reasoning Models**|Jungseob Lee et.al.|Hybrid reasoning models can answer directly or spend extra tokens on extended thinking. |**2026-10-07**|**TIPS: Topological Ill-Posedness Probing and Steering in Large Language Models**|Guangyu Jiang et.al.|Ill-posed questions, including those involving ambiguity, under-specification, or conflicting statements, may admit no valid answer or multiple plausible answers, posing a significant challenge for large language models (LLMs) despite their otherwise strong performance. |**2026-10-07**|**MORPH: Generative Retrieval via Diffusion Transformer with Metric-Ordered Sequence Training and Hybrid-Policy Preference Optimization**|Chenghao Liu et.al.|Embedding-based retrieval typically returns highest-scoring items, but many production scenarios require items that satisfy a target attribute while preserving a fine-grained pattern expressed by seed examples. |**2026-10-07**|**Look-Before-Move: Narrative-Grounded World Visual Attention in Dynamic 3D Story Worlds**|Jiaming Bian et.al.|As embodied AI and world models increasingly operate in dynamic 3D environments, visual perception must move beyond passively interpreting given observations toward actively deciding what to observe. |**2026-10-07**|**Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization**|Ke Zhang et.al.|Lean verifies that a generated declaration is well typed, but not that it states what the user intended. |**2026-10-07**|**Mastermind: Strategy-grounded Learning for Repository-Scale Vulnerability Reproduction**|Mingzhe Du et.al.|Repository-level vulnerability reproduction is a demanding software engineering (SE) task: an agent must inspect a codebase, infer the input grammar that reaches a vulnerable path, construct a proof-of-conceptv(PoC), and verify that the crash disappears on the patched build. |**2026-10-07**|**Subliminal Clocks: Latent Time Modelling in Diffusion Language Models**|Maximo Eduardo Rulli et.al.|Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models. |**2026-10-07**|**AgenticPD: A Stage-Aware Agentic Framework for Closed-Loop Physical Design Optimization**|Shuo Ren et.al.|Physical design quality-of-results (QoR) optimization is hard and expensive. |**2026-10-07**|**The Harness Effect: How Orchestration Design Sets the Token Economics of Enterprise Agentic AI**|Muayad Sayed Ali et.al.|Agentic AI development today runs on token maxing: buying capability with tokens -- longer reasoning traces, more turns, wider tool payloads, bigger replayed contexts -- so tokens per task grow faster than task value. |**2026-10-07**|**Measuring Intelligence Beyond Human Scale**|Jerry Han et.al.|How can we measure intelligence beyond human capability? |**2026-10-07**|**Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents**|Yike Wang et.al.|Harness evolution is an iterative search procedure that repeatedly evaluates and revises candidate harnesses used for LLM agents using task feedback. |**2026-10-07**|**What Keeps Vision-Language Models Looking at the Image?**|Hiroto Osaka et.al.|When do vision-language models need direct access to the image while generating an answer? |**2026-10-07**|**Cura 1T: Healthcare Foundation Model via Recursive Self-Improvement**|Haolin Chen et.al.|Healthcare spans high-stakes communication, expert reasoning, and workflow execution, yet specialized language models that cover these use cases together remain limited. |**2026-10-07**|**A Dual-Hypothesis Reasoning Framework for LLM Guardrails**|Md Asiful Islam et.al.|We propose ARBITER, a novel LLM guardrail framework that introduces two key ideas: (i) dual-hypothesis reasoning, a reasoning method for LLM guardrails that explicitly considers both safe and unsafe interpretations of a prompt before making a safety decision, and (ii) multi-component supervised fine-tuning (MC-SFT), a structured training loss for reasoning-based guardrails that decomposes LLM outputs into logical components and weights them according to their importance. |**2026-10-07**|**Neuro-Symbolic Meta-Policies for Temporal Knowledge-Graph Memory under Partial Observability**|Taewoon Kim et.al.|Partially observable reinforcement learning requires deciding what to retain, retrieve, and forget over time. |**2026-10-07**|**TILT: Model-Intrinsic Reward Alignment For Compositional Diffusion**|Debottam Dutta et.al.|Consider conditional generation $p(x \mid C=\{c_1, c_2, \dots c_k\})$ where $C$ is a prompt composed of multiple concepts $c_i$. |**2026-10-07**|**Deconstructing Off-Policy Ratios: Entropy-Normalized Trust Regions for Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning**|Guanqun Zhao et.al.|Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) accelerates large language model (LLM) post-training by overlapping rollout generation with policy optimization, but the resulting stale, off-policy data destabilizes optimization and can cause policy collapse. |**2026-10-07**|**Towards Trustworthy Physical Intelligence: From Theory to Practice Across Life Cycle**|Yang Wang et.al.|Physical intelligence refers to intelligence systems that understand, reason about, and act in accordance with the physical world and its underlying laws, dynamics, and constraints. |**2026-10-07**|**Dimensionality and Measurement Precision in HLE's Multiple-Choice Subset**|Mayank Sharma et.al.|Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is widely used to evaluate frontier language models. |**2026-10-07**|**SKILL-KD: Contrastive Skill Distillation for LLM Agents**|Qiming Shi et.al.|Skill-based prompting has become a practical mechanism for improving LLM agents, yet existing methods often treat skills as summaries of the agent's own experience or of successful demonstrations. |**2026-10-07**|**RA-CAD: Learning Post-Execution Critique for State-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation**|Shuhao Yan et.al.|Text-to-CAD generation translates natural-language design intent into editable and executable parametric computer-aided design (CAD) codes, reducing the expertise and effort required for manual modeling. |**2026-10-07**|**NxN E-valuation: Hypothesis Certification via a Conformal CRT Null**|Bin Wang et.al.|We propose NxN E-valuation, a handy, e-value-based hypothesis-certification algorithm that lets a hypothesis be verified without building any case-specific certification procedure---such as constructing a dedicated null hypothesis---as long as a large enough dataset is available. |**2026-10-07**|**The Value of a Prompt: An LLM-Relative Kolmogorov-Complexity Approach**|Rafael Pass et.al.|In a world where valuable artifacts are increasingly created, completed, or processed by LLMs, the central economic question is not only what the LLM can produce, but what \emph{value} remains in the inputs (i.e., the prompts) we provide to it. |**2026-10-07**|**CTIFoundry: An Agent-Native Corpus Scaffold for Cyber Threat Intelligence**|Yutong Cheng et.al.|Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) is increasingly consumed not by human analysts but by LLM agents that compose multi-step investigations at query time. |**2026-10-07**|**Hidden in the Request: Explaining Unethical LLM Compliance through Token Relevance**|Or Biton et.al.|Although Large Language Models (LLMs) are aligned to optimize for both helpfulness and harmlessness, these dual objectives may conflict, inevitably leading to alignment failures. |**2026-10-07**|**Towards Reliable, Generalizable, and Specific In-Context Knowledge Editing via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning**|Xuzhong Wang et.al.|Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful but limited by static parametric knowledge that becomes outdated once pretraining ends. |**2026-10-07**|**RealSWE: A Compositional Evaluation of Coding Agents under Realistic User Requests**|Gyuhyeong Kim et.al.|Coding agents are now commonly evaluated on the SWE-bench family of benchmarks, whose tasks are built from curated GitHub issues: long, structured, and information-rich.
